scheduler_findings.scope: Fully observed authenticated-worker intervals inside declared run08 machine-clock bracket
notes: sched_wakeup-to-switchin observes post-wakeup scheduling delay; sched_waking begins earlier in the wake path.
Runnable switchout uses R or R+; R+ has the trace preemption flag. Blocked-to-wakeup is not runnable delay.
Scheduled residency includes kernel and interrupt time and is not plug-in or SDK DSP duration.
Right-edge states have no manufactured duration through collector ACK.
Exact target duplicate events are skipped if present; stream-wide duplicates remain in separate audit.
18 waking events per worker begin before that worker switches out; waking-to-wakeup pairs are retained independently of switchout.

Ten identical rendered non-target switch records coincide with ten CPU-chain anomalies; they do not touch the authenticated worker streams or the longest native wake interval, and raw identity/origin remains unassigned.
Audio file byte marks, sparse bridge counters and one-second graph samples cannot map a zero span to a scheduler interval.
These observations neither prove nor exclude scheduling as the cause of the recorded zero spans.

The longest native wake interval remains scheduled to an unassigned task at kernel priority120 until a preemption-marked switch to the native worker at priority94; this is observed CPU scheduling context, not proof that the intervening task itself prevented preemption.

native_longest_wake_context.coverage_note: Categories are scheduled residency on the requested CPU; interrupt/NMI/softirq time is not separated and categories do not prove causal obstruction.
